title: How Active Noise Cancellation Works
summary: Active noise cancellation uses electronics and speakers to emit an inverted sound wave that destructively interferes with and cancels out unwanted background noise.

scenes.text: How do noise-cancelling headphones literally make sound disappear?
Sound travels as a pressure wave of alternating compressions and rarefactions.
Headphones emit a sound wave with the same amplitude but an inverted phase.
When the original noise wave is high, the cancelling wave is low.
In 1957, Willard Meeker developed an earmuff model with a 20 dB attenuation.
Periodic low-frequency sounds like engines are much easier to cancel than random noises.
scenes.reveal: Low frequencies have longer wavelengths that are simpler to invert.

scenes.text: Destructive interference turns two sound waves into silence.
